advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the docstrings with reality: the cell proves DC-shaped input handling under the default backend, not DC-backend selection; note the `jira-datacenter` assertion is trivially true because both families are `jira`.
evidence: fixture writes no config: store fixture only does `git init`, sets REBAR_ROOT, and `rebar.init_repo(repo_root=str(repo))` (lines 37-49) — no rebar.toml, no `[reconciler] backend = "jira-datacenter"`
adapters/jira/backend.py:150 `identity_family = "jira"` and adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py:211 `identity_family = "jira"` — both families are `jira`

apply_inbound_records.py:80 `return validate_creation_channel(getattr(backend, "identity_family", None) or backend.vendor)` — provider is the family `jira`, so a `jira-datacenter` mapping is never written by either backend
test docstring line 76-77 claims it says something 'about whether the DC path reaches it', and line 92-95 frames `jira-datacenter is None` as an anti-fork clause that could go red
advisory.finding: The module and test docstrings state the cell exercises 'whether the DC path reaches it' and treat `assert rebar.resolve_mapping("jira-datacenter", _DC_USER, ...) is None` as a load-bearing anti-fork guard, but the `store` fixture writes no `rebar.toml` selecting the `jira-datacenter` backend, and `_identity_provider_for` returns the family string `"jira"` for BOTH the Cloud and DC backends. The mint therefore always registers under `jira` and never under `jira-datacenter` regardless of which backend runs, so the anti-fork assertion is trivially true and the 'DC path' claim overstates what the test actually proves.
scenarios: A future reader trusts the docstring that this proves the DC-specific mint path; in fact the default Cloud `jira` backend is what is exercised and the `jira-datacenter` assertion can never fire for either backend

evidence: test: `air._ensure_inbound_assignee_identity({"name": _DC_USER, "displayName": _DC_USER}, repo_root=str(store))` then `assert minted is not None`

apply_inbound_records.py:131 `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort ghost mint; never fail the inbound apply` — every failure inside the mint (including backend construction) is swallowed and only logged at debug

failure message asserted: 'the production inbound mint did not register jira/... — the live oracle would be red for a real reason' attributes any None to the DC-shape guard, not to a swallowed backend-construction error
dropped.finding: `test_the_oracle_goes_green_on_the_real_dc_mint` drives `_ensure_inbound_assignee_identity`, which wraps its entire mint (including `select_backend(load_config())` backend construction) in a bare `except Exception` that swallows failures silently (apply_inbound_records.py:131). In this harness-free fresh store any environmental backend-construction failure (settings resolution, adapter import, etc.) makes the mint a no-op, so `resolve_mapping` returns None and the test fails with the message 'the production inbound mint did not register jira/...' — misattributing an environment/backend failure to the mint's DC-shape handling, which is exactly the diagnostic ambiguity the mutation check is meant to remove.
scenarios: CI/local runs where `select_backend(load_config())` cannot construct the default backend (missing adapter extra, settings resolution error) — the mint silently no-ops and this cell goes red with a misleading message
